meanings.note: Stronger than aimer for things. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to love'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'adoré').

examples.text: Je suis sérieuse. J'ai toujours adoré le cinéma.
examples.trans: I'm serious. I've always loved films.

meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
Je vais déjeuner. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').
Imperative used to encourage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'with', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
before the noun; bel before a vowel: un bel endroit

examples.text: Tu n'aimais pas Mandelieu? C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: Didn't you like Mandelieu? It's a lovely place.

meanings.note: beaucoup de + noun, with no article: beaucoup de travail

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many
meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'a lot'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: You know a lot of people.

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.
examples.trans: You know lots of people in film. You could help me.

meanings.note: Très bien = very well, fine. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
C'est bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'good'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Spoken French interj expression meaning 'bravo', common in natural conversation.

examples.trans: Well done, Mathias! Let me kiss you.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: Un prisonnier qui chante. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to sing'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'chanté').

examples.text: Un prisonnier qui chante, c'est très original.
examples.trans: A singing prisoner, that is very original.

examples.text: Charlotte Le Bon ne chante pas?
examples.trans: Charlotte Le Bon does not sing?

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
dire la vérité à quelqu'un = to tell someone the truth
dire à quelqu'un; dis-lui = tell her/him

examples.text: Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir.
Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: faire un disque = to record an album

examples.text: Nous allons faire un disque formidable.
examples.trans: We are going to make a wonderful record.
Her new album comes out tomorrow.

meanings.note: au début = at first, at the beginning

examples.trans: It's the start of the film.

examples.text: Ça dépend. Au début, j'étais dans les sous-vêtements des stars.
examples.trans: It depends. At first, I was in the stars' underwear department.

meanings.note: for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle
for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle

examples.text: Écoute, c'est une industrie, et elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: Listen, it's an industry, and it's full of sharks.

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

examples.trans: I've been waiting for an hour.

examples.text: Tu as fait quelque chose de formidable.
Super, Mathias! Tu as fait quelque chose de formidable. Bravo!
examples.trans: Great, Mathias! You did something wonderful. Well done!

meanings.note: c'est gentil = that's kind (of you)

examples.text: C'est gentil, mais je suis bien ici.
examples.trans: That's kind, but I'm fine here.

meanings.note: before the noun: une grande actrice = a great actress
Une grande star. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'big'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'big'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Nous avons presque perdu une grande star!
examples.trans: We almost lost a big star!

meanings.note: Informal praise. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'brilliant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'brilliant'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Oui! Elle s'appelle Armelle Borzek. Elle est géniale!
examples.trans: Yes! Her name is Armelle Borzek. She's brilliant!

meanings.note: Feminine: heureuse. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Je suis très heureux pour vous.
Voici Marie-Sophie Garnier, chef scénariste sur Heureux pour toujours.
examples.trans: This is Marie-Sophie Garnier, head screenwriter on Happy Ever After.

meanings.note: Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: c'est incroyable! = I can't believe it! / it's amazing!

examples.trans: You came! I can't believe it!

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Je te jure, c'est un film magnifique.
examples.trans: I swear, it's a wonderful film.

meanings.note: merci beaucoup = thank you very much

examples.text: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide précieuse aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your valuable help today.

examples.text: Je te dis mille fois merci pour ce beau rôle!
examples.trans: I thank you a thousand times for this great role!

meanings.note: Une jolie mélodie. Feminine noun ('la mélodie', plural 'les mélodies') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'melody'.

examples.trans: It is awesome, I love this melody.
This melody sticks in your head.

meanings.note: at the end of a sentence: super, non?
Tag at the end of a question. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: Passer par là: to go by there. Core French preposition meaning 'by', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Core French preposition meaning 'by', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Par exemple, le contrat de Canet.
Je peux regarder un contrat de Mathias? Celui de Canet, par exemple?
examples.trans: Can I look at one of Mathias's contracts? Canet's, for example?

meanings.note: Une belle prestation. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'acting performance, stage display'.

examples.text: Je suis époustouflé par sa prestation.
examples.trans: I am blown away by her performance.

meanings.note: Bonne soirée = have a nice evening. Feminine noun ('la soirée', plural 'les soirées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'evening'.
Une soirée = an evening party. Feminine noun ('la soirée', plural 'les soirées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'evening'.
agrees with the thing owned, not the owner

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: Un grand succès. Masculine noun ('le succès', plural 'les succès') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'success'.

examples.text: C'est le début d'un grand succès.
examples.trans: It is the beginning of a great success.

examples.text: Le film a eu un immense succès.
examples.trans: The film was a huge success.

examples.text: C'est un grand succès pour toi.
examples.trans: It is a great success for you.

meanings.note: Un timbre unique. Masculine noun ('le timbre', plural 'les timbres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'tone'.

examples.text: Oui, elle a un timbre unique.
examples.trans: Yes, she has a unique timbre.

examples.text: Il a un timbre de voix chaleureux.
examples.trans: He has a warm vocal timbre.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'very'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: Un talent unique. French relational/descriptive adjective derived from Latin adjectival roots.

examples.text: Oui, elle a un timbre unique.
examples.trans: Yes, she has a unique timbre.

examples.text: Pourtant, Samy a un talent unique!
examples.trans: Yet, Samy has a unique talent!

meanings.note: same form in singular and plural; à voix basse = in a low voice

examples.text: Sofia a vraiment une voix sublime.
examples.trans: Sofia truly has a sublime voice.

related.word: same form in singular and plural; à voix basse

Several people. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'you'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
je vous rappelle = I'll call you back
Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Tu crois vraiment qu'il va accepter ce rôle?
examples.trans: Do you really think he is going to accept this role?

examples.text: Je suis vraiment désolée pour ce petit retard.
examples.trans: I am truly sorry for this slight delay.

meanings.note: Être époustouflé par. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'blown away'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Je suis époustouflé par sa prestation.
examples.trans: I am blown away by her performance.
